rationale:
Issue #312 (labeled bug) reports that class selection with multi-byte characters silently returns zero matches on 2.8.1+ (`select("div.test-\u3042")` -> 0 elements). The minimized production patch is a single line in Element.hasClass(_:String) changing `className.count` (grapheme-cluster count) to `className.utf8.count`, which fixes the exact mismatch: the stored class attribute is a [UInt8] UTF-8 byte array whose `count` was compared against a grapheme count, so any non-ASCII class name hit the `len < wantLen` early `return false`. Cause, symptom, and fix line up. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test hunk from the same fixing commit (testHasClassDomMethods), which puts a supplementary-plane scalar (135361 = U+21001, 4 UTF-8 bytes) as the class and asserts hasClass returns true; it exercises the same byte-length-vs-character-length defect as the reported Japanese-character case and uses only pre-existing public API (hasClass, Attributes.put), so it compiles and runs on both revisions with no fix-only symbols. Strict machine evidence confirms build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential reproducing exactly the one declared selector, trigger.fixed_clean PASS, deterministic across 3 repetitions, and full_suite.fixed_all_green; post-minimization strict gates match the original (1 of 1 production hunk retained, validation PASS). The patch contains no refactor, formatting, feature, doc, or config change, and the test edit is isolated to the separate trigger patch. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so scinfu/swiftsoup#312 is not a duplicate and is the allowed root cause key.

Issue #312 (labeled bug) reports that class selection against non-ASCII class names regressed: `select("div.test-あ")` returns 0 matches on 2.8.1+. The minimized production patch is a single one-line correction in `Element.hasClass(_ className: String)` replacing `className.count` (grapheme-cluster count) with `className.utf8.count`, so the wanted length is measured in the same UTF-8 byte units as `classAtt: [UInt8]` — exactly the length-unit mismatch that makes multi-byte class names fail the `len < wantLen` and subsequent byte comparisons. `hasClass` is the mechanism behind the class selector reported in the issue, so issue, fix, and trigger describe one pre-existing defect. Traceability is fix_commit -> merged PR #320 ("closes #312") -> issue #312. The patch touches only Sources/Element.swift with one changed line: no refactor, formatting, feature, doc, or config change (original_hunk_count=1, retained=1, removed=0, post_minimization_validation PASS). The trigger is the unchanged upstream test portion of the same commit, appended to `testHasClassDomMethods`: it stores a supplementary-plane scalar (U+21001) as the class attribute and asserts `hasClass(s)` is true. It uses only APIs present on the buggy revision (`Attributes.put`, `Element.hasClass(String)`), so it compiles and runs on both revisions and is not a fix-only-API compile artifact; it exercises the same multi-byte-length bug class as the reported Japanese characters. Strict machine evidence reports build.both_versions PASS, trigger.buggy_differential reproduced on Tests/SwiftSoupTests/ElementTest.swift::testHasClassDomMethods, trigger.fixed_clean PASS, deterministic across 3 repetitions and 32 matrix runs, full_suite.fixed_all_green PASS, both pre- and post-minimization with no failed checks. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #312 is not a duplicate.
